purpose: Law-1 VISIBLE PARKED CHANNEL. Every finding this stage would otherwise have set aside is recorded here with a reason, an originating id and a confidence. Nothing was routed to /dev/null. Culling happens at triage (/ledger), never by withholding a finding from the run the human reviews. NOTE: zero items are here for low confidence or below-threshold quality - the whole list is either a C4 known-invalid CLASS awaiting the validity-checker's disposal, an out-of-first-party-scope root cause, or an unresolved hypothesis with no known consumer.
priorStages: The pattern-matcher emitted its own manualReview[] (6 items) and the code and econ scanners emitted theirs (5 and 4). Those are consolidated here so the human reads ONE parked list, and each item keeps its originating id.

items.title: Fee-on-transfer / weird-ERC20 handling on the stablecoin pull and on the phUSD forward
items.reason: C4 KNOWN-INVALID CLASS (fee-on-transfer and non-standard ERC20 out of scope unless explicitly in scope; USDT excepted). FLAGGED LIKELY-INVALID, NOT DROPPED - class disposal is the validity-checker's call, not the deduplicator's. Additionally: SA-003 sits INSIDE the delta window with materially changed context, so it is not carried as unchanged noise.
residualsThatTheClassDoesNotDispose: The pattern mostly FAILS CLOSED: :251 passes the REQUESTED stableAmount, and the conservation check at :254 makes a fee-skimming token revert StableNotDeposited, so the skew does not silently settle.
A rebasing-DOWN token makes the :246 pull fail rather than mis-credit - a DoS, not a leak.
A token whose fee is charged to the RECIPIENT of the minter's onward deposit skews the yield strategy's principal: ledger M-06 (ac6de2faade9adcd, wont-fix/parked) territory, adjacent not identical.

The phUSD transfer at :264 is not re-measured, and phUSD is FIRST-PARTY - the weird-ERC20 carve-out does not obviously reach a first-party token. This leg is NOT disposed by the C4 class and needs its own answer.

items.title: Approve race / forceApprove front-running on the minter allowance
items.reason: C4 KNOWN-INVALID (CLAUDE.md Known Invalid Findings lists 'Approve race condition / safeApprove front-running'). FLAGGED LIKELY-INVALID, NOT DROPPED, per the requirement that a skip be auditable.
items.twistConsidered: FOUND ABSENT. forceApprove(minter, stableAmount) at :247 is reset to 0 at :253 inside the same nonReentrant call, so no residual allowance persists between transactions and there is no window another transaction can interleave into. The only re-entry vector is the stablecoin's own transfer hook, blocked by the ReentrancyGuard (test/Annihilation.t.sol:386). No HM twist identified.

items.reason: C4 KNOWN-INVALID CLASS (weird ERC20) and moot in code for the pull leg (the ZeroAmount guard). FLAGGED, NOT DROPPED, because one of its three instances is inside the delta window and is NEWLY REACHABLE at mintedForStable == 0 - a state that could not be reached at c91bc1a.

If phUSD ever reverts on zero-value transfers, the zero-rate path becomes a revert rather than a silent settlement - which would be an accidental partial mitigation of R02 and should be verified, not assumed.

items.title: The depeg lever is neither fail-safe nor front-run-resistant: updateExchangeRate is onlyOwner, unbounded, untimelocked and MEMPOOL-VISIBLE, so a rate cut aimed at a depeg can be front-run by exactly the actors it targets
items.reason: PARKED, NOT MINTED, and NOT DROPPED. The econ agent deliberately declined to mint a second fingerprint because ECON-002's SETTLEMENT half is the same reachable end state as ECON-001 / 0ed1c6e3270816c5 and would double-count. The deduplicator does not overrule that. But the FRONT-RUNNING half is carried by NO ledger entry and NO other finding in this run, so leaving it only inside a merged entry's prose would make it invisible at triage. Parked here with its proposed basis so a human can decide to track it.
items.mechanism: A rate CUT takes effect only on inclusion, so a searcher who sees the pending cut annihilates first at the stale higher rate; a rate RAISE can be back-run. The lever therefore cannot outrun the arbitrage it exists to stop, while the two levers that CAN (pause / setStablecoinEnabled false, both hard reverts) are the ones an owner is least likely to reach for during ordinary rate management. Nothing on the annihilate path consults freshness, a timestamp or an external oracle (zero `block.` hits in src/).
items.twoSidedImpact: Downward: in-flight annihilations settle at the new lower rate against inert floors (the DEDUP-03-001 / R02 loss), at the moment the owner believed they were protecting users. Upward/stale: the window between a depeg and the owner's cut is an open arbitrage window (DEDUP-03-002).
items.whereItSurvivesRegardless: ECON-002's safeConfigGuidance is carried onto DEDUP-03-R02 so the operational advice reaches the owner even if this item is never minted.

items.title: PhusdStableMinter.mint has no non-zero-output guard of its own and will mint 0 phUSD for a real deposit, emitting PhUSDMinted as if normal
items.reason: OUT OF FIRST-PARTY SCOPE by the denylist (nested lib/), so it cannot be filed as an antimatter finding - but it is the SHARED ROOT CAUSE of DEDUP-03-R02 and the cleanest fix (one require) lives there, not in Antimatter. Parked visibly rather than dropped: any OTHER integrator of that minter inherits the identical hazard with NO Antimatter-style compensation at all, and nothing in this repo would ever surface it.
